items.title: Ray – an open-source AI financial advisor that runs in your terminal
items.raw_excerpt: I've been using this daily for 4 months and figured others might find it useful. This is my first open source project so would love any feedback. Ray connects to your bank via Plaid, stores everything in an encrypted local SQLite database, and lets you ask questions about your finances in natural language. No cloud, no account, your data is stored on your machine. Before anything reaches the LLM, all PII is stripped — your name, companies, transaction details are redacted and replaced with tokens, then rehydrated locally in the response. The AI never sees who you are.

excerpt_i18n.en: In the era of virtual agents, models have achieved leapfrog development by leveraging text, image, and video data, with language and visual intelligence maturing. However, when AI truly enters the physical world and aims to enable robots to work as dexterously as humans, it must handle diverse tasks in open-world scenarios with interaction. Thus, from a more fundamental capability perspective, embodied intelligence requires not just video or language-level skills, but the ability to perceive, act, and interact in real life, continuously thinking and iterating based on physical feedback. This means embodied intelligence must learn not from a video clip, but from natural and diverse Human Data in real life. Today, Jianzhi officially launches Gen DAS Dex (hereinafter referred to as Dex)—achieving high-precision reconstruction of full-modal perception and behavior of the human hand. Combined with Ego, it revolutionizes the "Human Data" paradigm, providing embodied intelligence with a dexterous behavioral data foundation that covers "head + hand" full-scene, fine-grained, and directly trainable scenarios. 01 Why does today’s embodied intelligence need a "hand" like Dex? The human hand, with its five fingers evolved over millions of years, consists of 27 bones, 34 muscles, and 24 degrees of freedom.
excerpt_i18n.es: En la era de los agentes virtuales, los modelos han logrado un desarrollo exponencial basándose en datos de texto, imágenes y vídeo, alcanzando la madurez en inteligencia lingüística y visual. Sin embargo, cuando la IA se adentra en el mundo físico y busca que los robots trabajen con la destreza humana, es necesario abordar tareas diversas en escenarios de mundo abierto con interacción. Por tanto, desde una perspectiva de capacidades más fundamentales, la inteligencia encarnada requiere no solo el nivel de vídeo/lenguaje, sino también la capacidad de percibir, actuar e interactuar en la vida real, reflexionando e iterando continuamente según la retroalimentación física. Esto implica que lo que la inteligencia encarnada debe aprender no es un simple vídeo, sino la vida real misma.

On April 2, 2026, during the ODCC Spring Plenary, the UALink ecosystem achieved a significant milestone. At the ODCC plenary meeting, Guo Liang, leader of the ODCC New Testing Group and senior engineer at the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, together with Wang Wei, ODCC executive committee member and senior director of Alibaba Cloud server R&D, jointly launched the UALink testing and verification service. They also disclosed the current internal test results of IP interoperability verification, marking the steady progress of UALink technology from standard specifications to industrial implementation.

The UALink testing and verification service released by ODCC is built on the UALink 1.0 specification, validating core functions such as interconnect IP, link protocols, transaction interactions, and data transmission. This ensures compatibility and interoperability between Switch chips and interface IP from different manufacturers in Scale Up networking. The UALink service provides a fair and impartial third-party technical testing and product certification service for the domestic UALink ecosystem, offering not only official technical specifications but also verified test results. It establishes a unified basis for UALink-compatible hardware R&D, third-party testing, procurement selection, and customer acceptance within the industry ecosystem.

In a video address during the launch ceremony, Kurtis, chairman of the UALink Alliance, stated: "Protocol verification is one of the keys to developing and establishing an open ecosystem. We thank ODCC for collaborating with the UALink Alliance to launch the UALink testing and verification service in China, ensuring through testing that UALink components are interoperable when connected."
excerpt_i18n.es: El 2 de abril de 2026, durante la asamblea de primavera de ODCC, el ecosistema UALink experimentó avances significativos. Además, revelaron los resultados actuales de las pruebas internas de interoperabilidad de IP, lo que marca que la tecnología UALink está avanzando firmemente desde la estandarización hacia su implementación industrial. El servicio de verificación y pruebas de UALink lanzado por ODCC se basa en la especificación UALink 1.0 y cubre aspectos clave como la interconexión de IP, protocolos de enlace, interacciones transaccionales y transferencia de datos.

excerpt_i18n.zh: 眼下，不少大厂人正经历着一种新旧焦虑交织的煎熬。 “以前总觉得自己是撑起部门业务的顶梁柱，直到上个月，我用 AI 工具半天就跑完了以前需要埋头干一周的分析报告，才发现这是降维打击啊。”近期，一位临近 35 岁的华东大厂战略人对雷峰网感慨道。 这两年，在一波波 AI 创新的冲击下，北京西二旗、后厂村与深圳深南大道的一栋栋大厂办公楼里的氛围已经变了：大家心里的“35 岁裁员危机”还没消散，一种新的，更迫在眉睫的焦虑——“AI 替代”又来了。 游戏设计师、前端程序员、测试员、客服……一批又一批的岗位遭遇AI引发的裁员重击。 而今年开年以来，各种办公智能体又将这种“AI 替代”的恐慌范围进一步扩大。 先是开源 AI 智能体 OpenClaw（小龙虾）引爆了全民学习热潮，紧接着巨头 Anthropic 带着 Claude Computer Use 技术袭来，用“视觉路线”接管电脑桌面，比小龙虾更激进。 “我现在不止焦虑 AI，”一位资深产品经理苦笑着说，“还焦虑那个比我更会用 AI 的年轻人。” 从比谁更能卷，到比谁更会用 Agent，人与人、厂与厂之间的竞争焦点已经开始转移，甚至深圳大厂的一些部门直接为程序员开出每人每月 4000 美元的 AI 工具报销额度，用 AI “武装到牙齿”。 打不过就加入，每个大厂人都在试图将 AI 工具变成救命稻草。但问题来了：面对当下大火的小龙虾和 Claude 等 Agent 工具，我们该选哪个，怎么用？ 远离开源：商业分析师林翰的谨慎与后怕 林翰大学毕业后进入华东一家互联网大厂，做云业务线的商业分析，至今已有七八年。 他告诉雷峰网，前段时间，当小龙虾、Claude Agent系列工具刷屏时，他的第一反应不是兴奋，而是心惊。看着那些几分钟就能生成复杂报表的工具，他想到的是：如果 AI 这么快，那还要他这个“老分析师”干什么？ 上周，他所在条线的销售
excerpt_i18n.en: Currently, many employees at major tech companies are grappling with a blend of old and new anxieties. "I used to think I was the backbone of my department's operations, but last month, I used an AI tool to complete an analytical report in half a day that previously took me a week of focused work. That's when I realized this is a dimensionality-reduction strike," a strategy professional from a major company in East China, nearing age 35, recently lamented to Leiphone. Over the past two years, amid waves of AI innovation, the atmosphere in the office buildings of major tech hubs like Beijing's Xierqi and Houchangcun, as well as Shenzhen's Shennan Avenue, has shifted. The lingering fear of "layoffs at age 35" has not yet dissipated, while a new, more imminent anxiety—"AI replacement"—has emerged. Game designers, front-end programmers, testers, customer service representatives... batch after batch of roles have been hit hard by AI-driven layoffs. Since the beginning of this year, various office AI agents have further expanded the scope of this "AI replacement" panic. First, the open-source AI agent OpenClaw sparked a nationwide learning frenzy, followed by the tech giant Anthropic introducing Claude Computer Use technology, which takes over computer desktops via a "visual route," even more aggressively than OpenClaw. "Now I'm not just anxious about AI," a senior product manager said with a wry smile, "but also about the younger colleagues who are better at using AI than I am." From competing over who can work harder to competing over who can better utilize AI agents, the focus of competition between individuals and companies has begun to shift. Even within some major Shenzhen-based firms...
excerpt_i18n.es: Actualmente, muchos empleados de grandes empresas están experimentando una angustia entre la ansiedad antigua y la nueva. "Antes siempre pensaba que era el pilar fundamental que sostenía las operaciones del departamento, hasta que el mes pasado, usando herramientas de IA, completé en medio día un informe de análisis que antes me llevaba una semana de trabajo intenso, y me di cuenta de que esto es un golpe demoledor", comentó recientemente un estratega de una gran empresa del este de China, próximo a los 35 años, a Leifeng.com. En los últimos dos años, bajo el impacto de sucesivas olas de innovación en IA, el ambiente en los edificios de oficinas de las grandes empresas en Xierqi y Houchangcun en Beijing, y en la Avenida Shennan en Shenzhen, ha cambiado: la "crisis de despidos a los 35 años" aún no se ha disipado en la mente de todos, y una nueva ansiedad, más apremiante —la "sustitución por IA"— ha llegado.
